text.t: Palmitic acid is a fatty acid: a long chain of carbon and hydrogen with an acid group on one end.
Its formula is C16H32O2, so the chain has 16 carbons.
The first carbon carries two oxygens, forming the carboxyl group that makes it an acid.
The rest is a hydrocarbon tail made only of carbon and hydrogen, which does not mix with water.
Every carbon-to-carbon bond in the tail is a single bond, so palmitic acid is a saturated fatty acid.
Long, straight saturated chains pack tightly, which is why fats rich in them are solid at room temperature.

does.t: Fatty acids are building blocks of fats, which cells use to store energy for the long term.
They are also part of phospholipids, major building blocks of cell membranes.

shape.t: A fat molecule is glycerol with three fatty acids attached.
A phospholipid has two fatty acids and a phosphate group on glycerol, giving it a water-loving end and two water-fearing tails.

text.t: Palmitic acid is derived from the palm tree, and it is also common in animal fats such as those in meat.
Fatty acid tails form the inside of the cell membrane.

wrong.t: Diets high in saturated fats might contribute to plaque building up in the arteries.

compare.t: Stretched out, palmitic acid measures about 2.2 nm from end to end.
That is a little longer than cholesterol in this gallery, which measures about 1.8 nm.

text.t: The acid end of the fatty acid.
The last carbon of the 16-carbon chain.
